chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Qasim ibn 'Urwa, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
I said to him, 'A man takes an oath not to approach his wife for three months.' He said, 'He said: It does not constitute 'ila' (oath of abstention) until he swears for more than four months.'

key_terms.إِيلَاء: Oath of abstention from conjugal relations

ai.seo_question: What is the minimum duration for an oath of abstention (ila) to be legally valid in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Baqir (AS) clarifies the jurisprudential threshold for *ila* (oath of abstention), specifying that a three-month vow is insufficient and must exceed four months to trigger the specific legal consequences. This distinction highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on precise temporal conditions in marital law, differentiating between a simple vow and the formal status of *ila* which involves a waiting period and potential divorce. The ruling underscores the balance between marital stability and the rights of both spouses within the framework of the Quranic injunctions on oaths.
